extracted.intended_audience: general readers; playwrights, screenwriters, directors, and students interested in David Mamet's methods and style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for writing and directing in the manner associated with David Mamet—particularly his approach to dialogue, dramatic plotting, and film storytelling (as summarized in his biography and writings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mamet speak (dialogue style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mamet's style of writing dialogue, marked by a cynical, street-smart edge, has come to be called 'Mamet speak.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue should be terse, cynical and street-smart; it often emphasizes rhythm, rapid exchange and an economy of words. The Wikipedia entry describes this trademark style and links it to his broader dramatic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize sound, logical plots over 'pretty' prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Mamet himself has criticized his (and other writers') tendency to write 'pretty' at the expense of sound, logical plots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an evaluative standard: favour clear, logically coherent plotting and dramatic cause-and-effect above ornate or 'pretty' writing. The biography notes Mamet's explicit criticism of sacrificing plot integrity for prettified language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Montage-driven film storytelling (show, don't narrate)
rubrics_metrics.description: In On Directing Film, Mamet advocates for a method of storytelling based on Eisenstein's montage theory, stating that the story should be told through the juxtaposition of uninflected images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the story through images and their juxtaposition; rely on cuts between scenes rather than exposition. Mamet urges directors to eliminate as much narration as possible and to let the juxtaposition of images convey meaning and advance the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus each scene on its point/objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Mamet urges directors to focus on getting the point of a scene across, rather than simply following a protagonist, or adding visually beautiful or intriguing shots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every scene should have a clear dramatic objective and communicate that objective directly. Avoid extraneous shots or pursuing visual beauty at the expense of scene clarity and storytelling purpose. Films should 'create order from disorder in search of the objective.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fast-paced dialogue and clear, simple imagery in screen work
rubrics_metrics.description: Mamet's signature style in commercial work and some films is described as fast-paced dialogue and clear, simple imagery (e.g., his Ford commercials featured this approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For screenwriting and direction, favour brisk pacing in exchanges and plain, unambiguous visual imagery that serves the story. This reinforces the montage/point-focused approach and Mamet's overall dramatic aesthetic.
